messages:
maria: Heads-up — CI on the ruby-sdk sample app started failing after the last bundler bump. locally i can reproduce with system ruby 2.7 while our dev guide assumes rbenv 3.1.

josh: oh interesting, what error do you see?

maria: gist of the failure: `bin/setup` has a shebang `#!/usr/bin/env ruby` and some binstubs end up using system gems, so bundler complains:
```
Your Ruby version is 2.7.0, but your Gemfile specified >= 3.0.0
```

maria: CI matrix includes `ruby:2.7` because we wanted wide coverage, but the Gemfile has `ruby '3.1.2'` now.

josh: hmm that mismatch is on us. Two options: loosen Gemfile ruby directive or tighten CI matrix. Which do we want for the sample app?

tim: for onboarding we should prefer matching the official SDK supported version (3.1). If people run system ruby older, it's okay as long as the quickstart explains `rbenv install 3.1.2`.

lane: small nit — the real problem I hit was `bin/console` and `bin/rails` being generated with absolute shebangs from my local bundler which points to rbenv shim. If CI uses docker + system ruby, the binstub shebangs are invalid. Best practice is to not check in generated binstubs for sampleapps.

maria: agreed. The sample app currently checks in `bin/*`. The PR I started removes binstubs and adds a `setup` script that runs `bundle install --binstubs tmp/bin` then symlinks. PR: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/1982>

josh: nice. Can we also add a short section in the README about `ruby` directive in Gemfile and recommended ruby versions? People keep hitting this when they copy the sample app into weird environments.

tim: +1 for README note. Also consider pinning CI to `3.1` and `3.2` only — coverage of 2.7 isn't that useful for new SDK users.

ci-bot: build #4821 failed on matrix: ruby:2.7 (see logs) :x:

maria: I pushed one more commit to the PR to remove checked-in binstubs and added a quick CI job that asserts `bin/*` are not checked in. snippet: `git ls-files -- "bin/*" | grep -q . && exit 1`

josh: can you add a minimal migration note in CHANGELOG or docs/DEVELOPMENT.md so maintainers know why we removed binstubs? PR reviewers often revert without context.

maria: good call — added a one-liner in DEVELOPMENT.md. Also added a fallback in `scripts/setup` that detects ruby < 3 and prints a clear message with `rbenv` or `asdf` instructions.

lane: unrelated — does the SDK auth retry parity test still pass after these changes? Some auth tests rely on a mock server binstub. If we remove binstubs we need to ensure test helpers still install any required executables into tmp paths.

maria: tested locally: auth tests still pass; the test harness installs the mock binary into `spec/support/bin` during CI setup. I'll add a CI smoke job that runs `bundle exec rspec spec/auth` in the PR.

josh: perfect. Reviewing now. quick request: change the commit message to reference the PR number and add `DX:` prefix so changelog generator picks it up.

maria: done. Thanks! :thumbsup:

ci-bot: build #4823 triggered for PR 1982 — running smoke auth tests :hourglass_flowing_sand:

tim: once merged we should also create a short community note in the ruby quickstart about shebang/binstub pitfalls. People on support keep asking the same question.

maria: will do after merge.

josh: approved in the PR, left one tiny nits comment.

maria: addressed nit, re-requesting review.

ci-bot: build #4823 succeeded — smoke tests passed :white_check_mark:

maria: merged. I'll open a follow-up issue to add the quickstart note and update the onboarding checklist for new contributors.

lane: awesome, thanks for moving quickly on this. :rocket:
